Step 1. String Theory: Take the G string and tie a loop big enough to fit the scroll of the violin.

Step 2. Pendulum Prelude: The violin should place its head in the loop, allowing it to swing like a pendulum.

Step 3. Violin Voyage: Rotate around gathering momentum while weaving two other lute strings through the F-holes of the violin.

Step 4. Final Fortissimo: Take the bow from the violin and play an arpeggio upon the lute. Do not tune-up; discordance is the end-goal.

10 REASONS TO HATE BARDDANCE

1. Always just a bunch of drunks dancing around like mindless fools. There's no MEANING to any of it.
2. They're playing it EVERYWHERE. Like, be original??!!
3. It is forced cheerfulness. People - this is basically socially acceptable MIND CONTROL. I will NOT be cheered against my will.
4. Eilistraee weeps every time someone requests Bard Dance AGAIN.

[The list continues on, mostly illegible after point 4 though you can pick out odd capitalised words like "CULT" and "SOULLESS" repeating over and over. The final entry is just a sketch of an angry face next to a smashed lute.]

Ten Sleeps To Go
Rehearsals went well today. Made it through all of our songs for the show next tenday, and Puddlepop stayed awake the whole time. We're ready for this!

Seven Sleeps To Go
We are not ready for this. Today, Melody took high offence at Scorchwood's "constructive suggestion" to smile more on stage, so she pinned him down and drew a grin across his face with the dyes from the face-painting kits.

Six Sleeps To Go
What do they put in those dyes? Soap, water, hours of scrubbing... and Scorchwood still looks like the saddest partially drawn clown from a child's nightmare.

Four Sleeps To Go
Rehearsals back on track. Another interruption today from a confused passer-by asking about our price-list for pruning and watering. Patiently explained Vicious Rockery is an ensemble, not a gardening business. He still looked confused as he left - as if the drums, violins, lutes stacked about were not enough to clue him in, or that we practise LOUDLY in a room next to the tavern's STAGE. Whatever. Maybe I should put another sign up.

Two Sleeps To Go
Two sleeps until performance night. Scorchwood looks like a wraith humped a bottle of dye and birthed a shadow-cursed clown baby on his face. At least the music sounds alright.

One Sleep To Go
One sleep before performance night. Lysandra has requested that she "sets down her lute" during the performance of Bard Dance, in protest against the "cult of soulless sell-out music spreading across the realm". What? Request was denied. I happen to quite like tips.

Performance Night
Success! Vicious Rockery always comes through when it counts, that's what makes us a team. Scorchwood's face cleared up (more or less), Lysandra only frowned a bit while we performed Bard Dance, and Melody was on form tonight with her crowd work. I'm writing in my diary as I listen to them downstairs now, retreating as I usually do once the post-performance celebrations start to get a bit too alcoholic for my liking. I can hear the familiar clinking sound of Puddplepop setting his bottles of mead out on the table - my cue to leave. Although, I think I just heard some patrons jeering at Scorchwood's name. And was that Melody coming to his defence? And that was definitely the sound of glass breaking. A lot of glass. And is that... crackling? Diary, I'm going to check they've not started another brawl - I'll be right

[The diary ends abruptly here.]

Ember's Lute v2.0

Hello and welcome to v2.0 of Ember's Lute :)

This mod is a port of Ember's Lute for the 'official' BG3 toolkit and post patch 7 mod.io curation.

If you have found your way here as a user of the original music performance mods on Nexus, please be aware this version is near enough a re-write from scratch! While intended to be like-for-like, there are a few differences in this version. However, should you find a favourite instrument or feature missing in this version, please feedback in the mod.io comments.

As usual, a huge thanks to you all for downloading, installing, and for your feedback and support.

Be well everyone ~Ariefel

Acquiring Instruments

[This section contains some very, very minor spoilers, such as the names of vendors and locations in Acts 2 and 3.]

On loading the game with this mod installed for the first time, you will have three items in your inventory: a lute, a scroll and this book.

The Lute of Musical Sprites is dropped straight into your inventory as a convenient way to quickly get started. This lute is just one of several instruments included in this mod.

To access the full set of instruments and items, use the Scroll of Summon Instrument to spawn a temporary chest straight into your inventory. Remove whichever instruments you want from the chest, and after 10 turns, the chest and any remaining content will disappear.

Vendor Locations

Alternatively, the instrument chest can be purchased from the following vendors:

Act 1: Arron the Halfing vendor in the Druid Grove.
Act 2: Harper Quartermaster at the Last Light Inn.
Act 3: The Chromatic Scale store in the Lower City.

Instrument Tips

Passives: After equipping an instrument, check the 'Passives' and 'Common' filters in the spell bar for new music spell containers and instrument passive toggles.

Themes: There are three themed instruments: Musical Sprites, Ensembles and "Annoying". They each offer a slightly different way to perform the BG3 bard songs: perform with support from sprites, summon a band, or just have a silly lute whistle along with your music! For more information, you can read the books included in each of the chest sub-containers.

Companions: To perform with companions instead of sprites or ensembles, you can use any of the instruments with the Musical Conductor passive. Cast the unlocked spell Share Musical Gifts, and each party member will auto-join music performances.

Passives (Again): Worth repeating! Most features in this mod can be toggled on or off e.g. the music VFX, whether the instrument sprites should be summoned to complete music, whether to add a "vocalist" sprite to the completed songs etc. And don't miss the instrument toggles for a convenient way to hear each of the BG3 bard songs with a variety of instrument combinations.

Have fun in BG3, mind the frogs (no spoilers), and I hope you enjoy the mod!

Musical Sprites Instruments

The instruments in this chest are inhabited by hundreds of small, playful musical sprites. They seem drawn to music performed on these instruments, appearing in a sudden swarm around the musician, dancing and circling. It is a mystery to me where they go once the music stops, or how they came to be attached to these instruments in the first place.

Ariefel's Notes on Sprite Summoning

The Musical Sprites instruments play "complete" songs: auto-summoning invisible instrument helpers whenever music is performed, which join in on other tracks (drum, violin, lyre, flute, etc.). This default auto-summoning behaviour can be toggled off in the Passives. Look for an icon of an open white music box named Sprite Summoning and disable it.

Ariefel's Notes on Musical Conducting

These instruments have the Musical Conductor passive, enabling the lead performer to toggle instrument tracks in and out of silence mid-performance. After equipping one of these instruments, look for the icons of music instruments in your Passives to enable and disable individual instrument music tracks.

Ariefel's Notes on Performing with Companions

On equipping an instrument, look for the Share Musical Gifts spell in your 'Common' filter. Casting this spell grants your party members Musical Proficiency, and enables them to automatically join in with musical performances. They can also be toggled in and out of performance with the instrument passive toggles.

Ariefel's Notes on Whistling

Whistling is supported, though by default it is disabled as part of the complete song performances. If you would like whistling to be included, you can toggle this on in the Passives. Look for the white music box named Sprite Summoning (Vocals) and enable it.

Ensemble Summoning Instruments

These instruments hold a fragile connection to the departed souls of long-forgotten musical ensembles, whom will readily answer the call to play music from those with the proficiency to lead the performance. The ensemble members are an eccentric bunch of characters, to say the least.

Arifel's Notes on Ensemble Instruments

Equipping one of these instruments grants a spell to summon an ensemble of musical performers. Once summoned, the ensemble members will automatically join any musical performances on an Ember's Lute instrument.

Ariefel's Notes on Musical Conducting

These instruments have the Musical Conductor passive, enabling the lead performer to toggle instrument tracks in and out of silence mid-performance. After equipping one of these instruments, look for the icons of music instruments in your Passives to enable and disable individual instrument music tracks.

These toggles will work with the summoned ensemble members, based on which instrument they have equipped.

Annoying Lutes

This lute is a contemptible jerk.

[You flip the page over looking for further notes, but that seems to be whole of it.]

Ariefel's Notes on Annoying Lutes

The lutes in this chest are inhabited by an agent of chaos. Equipping one grants a handful of spells and abilities aimed at causing mischief and mayhem.

That is all you really need to know. That, and they like to whistle.

Ariefel's Notes on Instrument Varnishes

The purpose of an instrument varnish is to grant the spells, statuses and passives of Ember's instruments, to any common instrument of Faerûn.

To apply a varnish, simply equip the instrument you want to convert, and then Use the varnish. The effects will wear off if the varnished instrument is unequipped.

Varnishes should work on most custom and modded instruments, as well as vanilla instruments.

n.b. Varnishes cannot be used to mix and match different Ember's Lute instrument themes on the same instrument.

Ember's Lute - FAQ and Troubleshooting

This book is a compilation of frequently asked questions and common troubleshooting issues with this mod and with BG3 modding in general, as of June 2025. Keep in mind when reviewing this in-game book for advice and be aware you may find more up to date guides online.

The Mod Won't Update

Issues relating to updating BG3 mods are most commonly experienced by players using the in-game Mod Manager. There are a couple of ways it presents, such as a Blue update arrow that doesn't disappear, or a system error is thrown with a locked file message.

If you are a PC user, and see the file locked error when attempting an update of the mod, then disable the mod in the Mod Manager menu. Do not unsubscribe, just uncheck the green box and then quit BG3. Re-launch BG3. With the mod disabled on startup of BG3, you should now be able to update it to the latest version and then re-enable it to load your Save game.

If you are experiencing the persistent blue arrow, then this is sometimes a result of the BG3 Mod Manager becoming out of sync with mod.io. Follow the same steps as for the locked file issue (disable the mod in Mod Manager, restart BG3). Once back in the Mod Manager, Unsubscribe from the affected mod and then exit BG3.

PC users can also try checking your BG3 Mods folder in Windows Explorer and confirming there are no older versions of the mod left in the folder. If you find any, delete them all manually.

Now launch BG3. BG3 may automatically download the latest version of the mod, but if not, go to the Mod Manager and re-download again. You should now have the latest version installed and enabled.

The Mod Won't Unsubscribe

This issue is the same root cause as the update issues: either a locking file or a sync issue with mod.io. Follow the steps for the answer above and adjust the final steps to unsubscribe rather than update or re-download the mod.

No Crowd Reactions for Performances

This is a symptom of a common way BG3 mods can inadvertently break the brittle BG3 music performance system in game. It can be caused by any mod which is applying regular statuses to your player character (such as class, spell or framework mods).

If you have a mod installed which is breaking music statuses, then the other symptom you will observe is that playing music on a vanilla (non-modded base game) instrument will be interrupted after a few seconds.

Unfortunately, there is no quick and easy way to identify which mod is causing the interruptions, other than trial and error (adding mods in one by one until the interruptions can be replicated). It is unlikely to be a cosmetic mod. Framework mods, class mods, or those that add complex new spells may be the place to begin if you are considering this approach.

If you are a PC user, then you can try installing the Optional Files mod "musicperformanceworkaround" from the Ember's Lute Nexusmods page:

https://www.nexusmods.com/baldursgate3/mods/9678?tab=files

You may need to experiment with Load Order, but sometimes this mod can prevent the interruptions. It is a simple override mod, and is safe to be added or removed at any point in your campaign.

Finally, here's a link to an article on this common issue with a bit more information:

https://www.nexusmods.com/baldursgate3/articles/796.

How Do I Uninstall this Mod?

This answer assumes "uninstall" means to erase the mod from a Save campaign. See the answer above for an issue related to "Unsubscribing" the mod via the BG3 Mod Manager.

For console users: Once you Save your campaign with a mod enabled, BG3 will require the mod to be active and enabled from that Save point onwards in the campaign. In order to continue the campaign after removing this mod via the in-game Mod Manager, you will need to load a Save game from before this mod was added. I therefore recommend that you trial this mod and decide whether you wish to keep it in your campaign before progressing several hours further into the story.

For PC users: In the Ember's Lute Mod Preferences spell container, there is a spell to Clean Mod Items. This is a pre-requisite for removing a mod with custom items and statuses mid-campaign. Refer to this spell for more detailed instructions, limitations and guidance.

Crash to Desktop Equipping an Instrument

A consistent and repeatable crash to desktop or main menu is due to missing mod dependencies. If you are using Haunted Instruments or Celestial Instruments, then make sure the dependent Ember's Lute mod is enabled as well.

You can also change the load order in BG3 by disabling and re-enabling the Haunted and Celestial mods in Mod Manager. This forces BG3 to re-write the mod order list, placing them below their dependency mod, Ember's Lute.

My Question Isn't Answered Here

BG3 has an in-game feature which allows the reporting of mod issues. Please be as specific as possible when reporting an issue, and include anything that might be relevant such as which instrument was equipped, which song was being performed etc.

The most common root causes of user mod issues are the BG3 Mod Manager or conflicting behaviour with another mod. Guidance can be offered via the Mod page on Nexus or Mod.io, but resolutions usually require information and a dialogue with the user to troubleshoot their specific setup.

FAO: CONSOLE PLAYERS

It is NOT POSSIBLE to remove mods mid-campaign on console. The BG3 Mod Manager will prevent a Save from being loaded if it detects a mod is missing.

REMOVING A MOD

Mods that add custom items, statuses and spells in BG3 are not trivial to remove mid-campaign. Larian DOES NOT SUPPORT removing mods mid-campaign, and actively blocks it on console.

This item clean-up is offered only to help the player with the removal of Ember's Lute mods if required. No guarantee is made that it will work for 100% of campaigns, 100% of the time. You choose to remove a mod at your own risk!

SAVE YOUR GAME FIRST

It is strongly recommended to create a Save restore point before proceeding with this item clean up.

Would you like to continue to review the next (and final) information message?

CAVEAT

This item clean up is not able to locate and erase any custom items from the Ember's Lute mods that have been lost or dropped in the world. It will only work on custom items kept in party inventories or in the Camp Chest.

CONTINUE?

Choosing "Yes" will delete all Ember's Lute mod items in your party inventories and the Camp Chest, and from any traders you have interacted with. This operation is not reversible.

Continue?

When re-loading the Save, you will still see a warning from BG3 that a required mod is missing, but choose continue anyway. If successful, you will be able to load your Save.

If not, you will land back at the BG3 Main Menu and will need to re-enable the mods to continue again.

PLEASE NOTE

When re-loading the Save, you will still see a warning from BG3 that a required mod is missing, but choose continue anyway. If successful, you will be able to load your Save.

If not, you will land back at the BG3 Main Menu and will need to re-enable the mods to continue again.

IF IT DOES NOT WORK

It means your campaign has items or statuses woven deeper into Faerûn than this clean-up tool can reach.

For a more thorough mod uninstaller, seek out Volitio's BG3 Mod Uninstaller on https://www.nexusmods.com. This is an excellent and highly recommended tool with very high success rates for mod removal.

Ember's Lute v3.0 Changelog

This book contains a short summary of the main updates included in version 3 of Ember's Lute.

Showmanship
Increase Showmanship charges while performing music, and the crowds gathered will respond by demonstrating their appreciation through clapping, dancing, throwing flowers, coins or other things.

Performing in Camp
Companions gathered to listen to the music will have a little more animated variety than the default shuffle and head bobbing.

Performance Rewards
While performing music to crowds outside of camp, there is a chance that at the end of a performance you'll find a gift placed in your backpack. All donations are made anonymously! Some rewards which can be used in combat are locked behind character level and other rewards require a story condition to first be met.

Sheet Music
There are 5 BG3 songs to be learned, to add to your performing reportoire, each with a unique VFX. Find and read sheet music to learn the song. These songs use the standard BG3 music mechanics for music game state integration, so by default there are location constraints on where they can be performed. This constraint can optionally be removed - see Mod Preferences.

Mod Preferences
On equipping any instrument from Ember's Lute, the character will be given a spell container that enables a number of preferences to be enabled or disabled. For those updating from version 2, note that many of the "config" toggles have been relocated here, to declutter the wheels in controller UI mode.

Also note that preferences are set per character, meaning you may have different preferences for different characters if you like. There is also a spell included to copy preferences to all other members of the team.

Mod Item Clean Up
Also found in the preferences spell container, is a spell that will find and destroy all custom items from the Ember's Lute mods. This is included mainly for PC players, as a pre-requisite to removing a mod mid-campaign. Save your game and read the information pop-up carefully before proceeding!

Crowd Reaction Resilience
Bard crowd reactions have been de-coupled from the brittle vanilla BG3 crowd reaction statuses. Meaning: if you have a mod which is unintentionally removing the vanilla crowd reaction statuses, then crowds gathered while playing on custom instruments from Ember's Lute should no longer be impacted.

Keep on Entertaining...
Crowds will only disperse when you fully end the performance by moving - or for custom performances, moving outside the golden "ring". This means you can switch between songs and continue to entertain your gathered fans.

NPC Bards Join In
Version 3 now supports NPC bards automatically joining in with the performance when playing on an instrument from Ember's Lute. If the Musical Conductor aura is up, then they can also be toggled in and out of the performance by instrument type as per other Musical Sprites and Spirits.

Ember's Lute v3.0

Welcome to version 3 of Ember's Lute!

In this book, you will find a quick guide on how to get started, as well as some headlines on the major changes between version 2 and version 3. You can also read the version changelog dropped into your inventory for more details.

Whether you're a new mod user or updating from version 2, I'd like to thank you for downloading, installing, and for your feedback and support!

New in Version 3

~ Custom crowd reactions!
~ Rewards for performing music!
~ Find and learn 5 new performable single-track songs!
~ Enhanced mod preferences!

Acquiring Instruments

[This section contains some very, very minor spoilers, such as the names of vendors and locations in Acts 2 and 3.]

On loading the game with this mod installed for the first time, you will have three items in your inventory: a lute, a scroll and this book.

The Lute of Musical Sprites is dropped straight into your inventory as a convenient way to quickly get started. This lute is just one of several instruments included in this mod.

To access the full set of instruments and items, use the Scroll of Summon Instrument to spawn a temporary chest straight into your inventory. Remove whichever instruments you want from the chest, and after 10 turns, the chest and any remaining content will disappear.

Vendor Locations

Alternatively, the instrument chest can be purchased from the following vendors:

Act 1: Arron the Halfing vendor in the Druid Grove.
Act 2: Harper Quartermaster at the Last Light Inn.
Act 3: The Chromatic Scale store in the Lower City.

Instrument Tips

Passives: After equipping an instrument, check the 'Passives' and 'Common' filters in the spell bar for new music spell containers and instrument passive toggles. For those using the Controller UI, you will find both the passive toggles and spell containers in the UI wheels.

Themes: There are three themed instruments: Musical Sprites, Ensembles and "Annoying". They each offer a slightly different way to perform the BG3 bard songs: perform with support from sprites, summon a band, or just have a silly lute whistle along with your music! For more information, you can read the books included in the summonable instrument chest.

Companions: To perform with companions instead of sprites or ensembles, you can use any of the instruments with the Musical Conductor passive. Cast the unlocked spell Share Musical Gifts, and each party member will auto-join music performances.

Preferences: Many features in this mod can be toggled on or off per character e.g. the music VFX, whether, whether to add a "vocalist" sprite to the completed songs, whether to enable or disable the custom crowd reactions etc. Note that in version 3 of this mod, preferences that were previously passive toggles have been moved to a new spell container, Ember's Lute - Mod Preferences.

Sheet music for BG3 songs can be found around Faerûn. If a character with Musical Proficiency reads the sheet music, they can learn how to perform the song.

Sheet music might also be acquired as a reward for musical performances, once certain story conditions have been met.

Notes on Custom Performances
The custom performances in this mod utilise the vanilla BG3 music events. This was a choice made to support compatibility, however for a variety of technical reasons this book will not go into, there are a few compromises to be aware of.

Location Restrictions
Some music events are linked to scripted story events, meaning that once certain story conditions are met, they will behave differently in certain areas. For example, they may only play silence in certain locations.

To simplify unexpected behaviour, the custom performances are by default restricted to in camp only. You can however optionally remove this location constraint in the preferences for the mod.

Cast the spell named Disable Safe Zones to remove the performance location restrictions.

Switching Character Control
Some music events are linked to game states, such as combat mode or "drive" states. BG3 resets its state when a player switches character control. What this means is that certain songs will stop playing music if you take control of another party member or summon.

The sheet music will highlight the songs with this behaviour as it is understandably confusing to the player to see performances end if switching character control!

Epilogue
The custom performances will not be available in the Epilogue. This book will not go into the reason why due to potential spoilers, other than to say more mod work would be required to support the music event interactions.

Ember's Lute v3.0.5 Changelog

The Ember's Lute music mod and its two add-ons, Celestial and Haunted Instruments, are all over a year old! Being a bit of a passion project of mine, I have not left them alone during that period either. Inevitably, scope has increased and with it, complexity.

This update focuses on changes to behaviours and interactions between the music mod spells, abilities and instruments across the add-ons, with a view to improving overall stability. Some of these changes required constraints introducing to prevent interactions that can (possibly) lead to instability, but there are no fundamental changes to the core of what the music mods are about.

By intentional design, all changes summarised apply only to Ember's Lute custom music spells and performances. There are no changes to how vanilla instruments behave, nor to the vanilla music performances. These should continue to work alongside the customisations in this mod, as per a vanilla BG3 game.

On First Load After Updating
Depending on what state your game is in when you loaded with this update, you may have noticed a few statuses are dropped automatically, or an instrument or piece of mod equipment removed automatically. This is just a one-time only effect to ensure some attributes and flags are cleared off characters and future loads will not trigger repeats of this. Impacted areas are:

- Share Musical Gifts status (auto-removed)
- Incorrectly varnished instruments (auto-unequipped)
- Celestial underwear equipment with wings (auto-unequipped)

Lead Musical Performers
Many of the stability changes are based around ensuring there is at most one lead musical performer. If another character in your party starts a new musical performance while within range of an active musical performance, they will now join the performance (i.e. they will no longer trigger their own Musical Conductor aura).

n.b. You can still "join" with a completely different song to the active performance if you are a fan of cacophony... Its your ears, not mine!

Lead Musical Performers - Out of Range
If there is an active musical performance and your current character is out of range of this performance, the music spells will be disabled with a message that politely tells you to get closer if you want to join in.

1. I have noticed the container spell can sometimes not re-enable itself (not sure if logic bug or UI lag at this point), but you can usually still click through the spell container to the spells if needed, even if the container icon presents as greyed-out.

Share Musical Gifts
The behaviour of Share Musical Gifts status was found to have been interacting with the custom music auras in a way that could sometimes result in instability. It has been changed/fixed in the following ways:

1. It will no longer bring characters automatically into musical performances while in combat.
2. It will no longer have any effect on characters who are leading a musical performance, or have an active conductor aura.
3. It is now a spell container with additional spells to apply Honorary Musical Spirit status to a single target, and to remove from a target.

Instrument Varnish Fixes
At some point I broke the constraints on instrument varnishes which stopped them from being applied to other sprites / spirits / ensemble instruments. There was good reason for this constraint, so now it is back!

1. While testing I noticed it was also still possible to, um, varnish yourself (no instrument equipped). I thought about blocking this, but also noticed that it "kind of" seemed to work. Caveat: I say "it works", I have not extensively tested it, so use this mode as a lead vocalist at your own risk!

Music Combat Auras
Similarly to the the lead performer changes, if you are performing music in combat using the combat spells, you should now be limited to 1 lead performer and 1 main music combat aura. Other party members can join in the combat music performance, and if they do, will create a party buff at the end of every combat round.

1. The combat "support" buff is purposefully weaker than the main combat aura, so there is less reason to use it as support performers will still be locked down in the same way as the lead performer. However, if you especially want a party full of music players supporting your main fighter (for example), you can still do this - they just won't all be generating the main combat auras.
